findings.title: Quiescent Sphericity and Convective Absence in Microgravity
findings.description: In the absence of buoyancy-driven natural convection, isolated fuel droplets burn with near-perfect spherical symmetry. The absence of rising buoyant plumes significantly alters temperature fields and oxidizer transport mechanisms.
findings.quantitative_result: Flame sphericity index > 0.98; peak gas temperatures 150-250 K lower than buoyant counterparts
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Standard terrestrial flame sensors calibrated for upward plume thermal signatures fail to detect spherical fires.

findings.title: Cool Flame Burning Sustained Below Classical Flammability Limits
findings.description: After apparent radiative extinction of the hot visible flame, droplet burning continues in a low-temperature 'cool flame' chemical regime driven by low-temperature hydrocarbon oxidation pathways.
findings.quantitative_result: Cool flame temperatures range between 600 K - 800 K; sustained invisible reaction lasts up to 40 seconds post-extinction
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Fires may appear fully extinguished while continuing to release carbon monoxide, formaldehyde, and volatile intermediates.

findings.title: Concurrent Solid Fuel Flame Spread Reduction
findings.description: Concurrent flame spread rates over thin solid fuels (such as PMMA and cotton blends) in microgravity are 30% to 60% lower than corresponding normal-gravity upward spread tests.
findings.quantitative_result: Spread rates between 0.3 mm/s and 1.8 mm/s vs 2.5 mm/s on Earth
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Slower fire spread provides extended crew egress time, but masks rapid internal thermal accumulation in confined spaces.

findings.title: Opposed-Flow Extinction Boundary Shift
findings.description: In opposed flow, flame stabilization exhibits a dual extinction limit: blowing extinction at high velocity (>35 cm/s) and radiative quenching at extremely low velocity (<2 cm/s).
findings.quantitative_result: Radiative extinction boundary reached at 1.5 cm/s forced air velocity at 21% O2
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Simply reducing cabin ventilation can extinguish opposed-flow flames through radiative heat loss without expending chemical suppressants.

findings.title: Large-Scale Fire Propagation Dynamics in Cygnus Cargo Craft
findings.description: First large-scale fire experiment inside an uncrewed operational spacecraft confirmed that continuous cotton-fiberglass fabric samples propagate flame stably without buoyant lifting or tearing.
findings.quantitative_result: Steady flame spread velocity of 0.8 cm/s; peak heat release reached 45 kW
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Demonstrates that terrestrial small-scale NASA STD-6001 Test 1 flammability tests underestimate real space vehicle fire propagation rates.

findings.title: Oxygen Depletion and Pressure Drop in Sealed Spacecraft Cabin
findings.description: Evaluated multiple fuel samples under varying atmospheric pressures and oxygen fractions during spacecraft departure trajectory.
findings.quantitative_result: Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) shifts by 2.5% to 4.0% depending on ambient pressure level
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Exploration atmospheres (e.g., 34% O2 at 56 kPa for Artemis Moon missions) increase material flammability despite lower total pressure.

findings.title: Enhanced Soot Formation and Radiative Feedback
findings.description: Because residence times of hydrocarbon intermediates are extended in microgravity laminar coflow flames, soot agglomeration increases by over 100% relative to 1g conditions.
findings.quantitative_result: Soot volume fraction f_v doubled; radiative heat emission increased by 45%
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Higher soot levels cause severe optical obscuration, blinding navigation optics, and rapidly clogging Environmental Control and Life Support (ECLSS) filters.

findings.title: Smoke Particle Size Distribution Shift Toward Larger Agglomerates
findings.description: Absence of buoyant shear forces allows soot primary spheres to aggregate into elongated chain networks with aerodynamic diameters 3-5 times larger than in 1g.
findings.quantitative_result: Mean aggregate radius of gyration R_g increased from 85 nm (1g) to 320 nm (0g)
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Ionization smoke detectors have reduced sensitivity to larger agglomerates; light-scattering photoelectric detectors perform far better in space.

findings.title: Gaseous Fuel Burning Rate Emulation and Boundary Layer Attachment
findings.description: A flat porous burner emitting controlled gaseous fuel simulated solid material burning behavior without surface char degradation complexities.
findings.quantitative_result: Flame standoff distance increased by 300% compared to 1g boundary layers
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Flames stand farther off surfaces in microgravity, transferring less heat directly back to the condensed phase in quiescent atmospheres.

findings.title: Electric Field Manipulation and Flame Extinction Control
findings.description: Application of non-uniform electrostatic fields (up to 5 kV) exerted ionic wind body forces on chemi-ions, allowing remote flame deflection and rapid extinction.
findings.quantitative_result: Flame lift-off and extinction achieved in under 1.2 seconds without chemical extinguishant
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Provides a non-toxic, non-contaminating suppression mechanism for avionics bays and enclosed instrument electronics.

findings.title: Limiting Oxygen Index of Nomex and Advanced Polyamides
findings.description: Evaluated the flammability boundaries of flame-retardant synthetic aramids under low forced airflow in microgravity.
findings.quantitative_result: Nomex self-extinguishes below 26.5% O2 at 101 kPa in microgravity
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Nomex remains completely self-extinguishing in standard ISS air (21% O2), but becomes combustible in lunar suit airlock staging areas (up to 30% O2).

findings.title: Charring Polymer Ignition Delays and Crust Rupturing
findings.description: Thick charring polymers in microgravity form insulating superficial char caps that periodically rupture due to internal gas pressurization, ejecting hot pyrolyzing sparks.
findings.quantitative_result: Internal pressure buildup exceeds 12 kPa prior to char eruptive venting
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Secondary fire ignition risk across habitat modules caused by drifting glowing embers unconstrained by gravity.

findings.title: Water Mist Extinguishment Efficiency in Confined Geometries
findings.description: Fine atomized water droplets (10-50 µm) demonstrate exceptional heat absorption in microgravity because droplets remain suspended rather than settling downward.
findings.quantitative_result: Flame extinguishment achieved with 55% less water volume than required in 1g tests
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Water mist is an ideal non-halon suppression agent that protects crew respiratory health and avoids toxic agent cleanup.

findings.title: Smoldering Transition to Flaming Under Forced Ventilation
findings.description: Open-cell polyurethane foam samples undergoing quiescent smoldering rapidly transitioned to open flaming when ventilation was restored to nominal cabin flow rates.
findings.quantitative_result: Transition time from smolder to vigorous flame: 4.8 seconds after flow resumption
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Cabin ventilation must NEVER be re-engaged following a suspected fire until thermal imaging verifies complete cooling below pyrolysis thresholds.

findings.title: Lunar Gravity (0.16g) Combustion Behavior on Parabolic Flights
findings.description: Combustion spread in lunar gravity (0.16g) is often more hazardous than either 0g or 1g, as partial buoyancy supplies fresh oxidizer while heat losses remain modest.
findings.quantitative_result: Flame spread rate at 0.16g peaked 20% higher than identical samples at 0g under 5 cm/s flow
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Lunar base fire protection standards cannot simply interpolate between 0g ISS and 1g Earth data.

findings.title: Martian Gravity (0.38g) and CO2 Atmosphere Interactions
findings.description: Studied flame anchoring and spread at 0.38g in environments representing surface habitat interior conditions with accidental external CO2 ingress.
findings.quantitative_result: Critical flame spread velocity 1.4 mm/s; lower flammability limit shifts by +1.8% O2
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Habitats on Mars experience moderate buoyancy, requiring directional ventilation baffles near sleeping quarters.

findings.title: Combustion of Wire Insulation in Overheated Cable Harnesses
findings.description: Electrical wire bundles with PTFE (Teflon) and ETFE (Tefzel) insulations subject to high current overloads generate toxic pyrolyzates before visible flame ignition.
findings.quantitative_result: Hydrogen fluoride (HF) and carbonyl fluoride (COF2) outgassing detected 45s before ignition
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Off-gas chemical trace sensors provide earlier warning of harness failure than conventional particulate detectors.

findings.title: CO2 Dilution Extinction Curves in Microgravity
findings.description: Carbon dioxide is substantially more effective at radiative flame suppression in microgravity because trapped hot CO2 emits thermal radiation omnidirectionally, cooling the flame zone.
findings.quantitative_result: 18% lower CO2 concentration needed for flame extinction in 0g than in 1g
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Portable CO2 fire extinguishers currently deployed on ISS are highly effective, but require crew breathing mask donning immediately.

findings.title: Teflon (PTFE) Thermal Decomposition Pathways in Reduced Gravity
findings.description: PTFE decomposes endothermically into gaseous fluorocarbon monomers; in microgravity, dense fluorocarbon vapors blanket the surface, delaying ignition until high radiant flux is reached.
findings.quantitative_result: Critical heat flux for ignition: 32 kW/m2 in microgravity vs 26 kW/m2 in Earth gravity
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: PTFE remains one of the safest insulation polymers for spaceflight, provided high-temperature gas traps are installed.

findings.title: Surface Orientation Independence of Flame Spread
findings.description: Unlike Earth fires where upward spread is an order of magnitude faster than downward spread, microgravity flame spread speed is entirely governed by airflow vector relative to the fuel surface.
findings.quantitative_result: Variance across orientations < 4% (compared to > 800% variance in 1g)
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Fire spread direction in spacecraft cannot be predicted by vertical geometry; ductwork and ventilation maps are the sole determinants.

findings.title: Soot Deposition on Radiative Heat Exchangers
findings.description: Soot particles generated in microgravity exhibit thermophoretic migration toward cold habitat hull panels and radiator heat exchangers, degrading radiative emissivity.
findings.quantitative_result: Thermal emissivity reduced by 28% after single small soot deposition event
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Even small uncontained flame events jeopardize habitat thermal balance by fouling active cooling surfaces.

findings.title: Low-Speed Quenching Distance Expansion
findings.description: Spherical diffusion flames expand significantly, with flame zone quenching distances from metallic surfaces increasing by a factor of 2.5 to 3.0.
findings.quantitative_result: Quenching distance expanded from 1.8 mm (1g) to 5.2 mm (0g)
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Terrestrial flame arrestors and mesh screens may allow microgravity flames to penetrate through gaps that are safe on Earth.

findings.title: Flammability of 3D-Printed Thermoplastics (Ultem and PEEK)
findings.description: Evaluated 3D printed PEEK and Ultem 9085 flight parts. Layer orientation and print porosity introduce microscopic oxygen diffusion channels that accelerate flame spread along layer seams.
findings.quantitative_result: Flame spread along print layer axis was 22% faster than perpendicular to layers
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Spacecraft 3D printed components must align print layers perpendicular to expected cabin ventilation flow vectors.

findings.title: Silicone Elastomer Sealant Combustion and Silica Ash Shedding
findings.description: Combustion of silicone seals produces a brittle white silicon dioxide (SiO2) ash layer. In 0g, this ash crust floats freely as abrasive airborne particles.
findings.quantitative_result: 100% of silica ash released into circulation stream without gravitational settling
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Floating silica ash poses immediate optical and lung damage hazards to astronauts during and after fire events.

findings.title: Toxic Gas Yield Ratio: CO to CO2 in Under-Ventilated Microgravity Fires
findings.description: Due to restricted oxygen diffusion in microgravity combustion, the CO/CO2 yield ratio increases dramatically, generating lethal concentrations of carbon monoxide rapidly.
findings.quantitative_result: CO/CO2 mass ratio rose from 0.04 (well-ventilated 1g) to 0.28 (microgravity enclosure)
findings.implications_for_spacecraft: Crew incapacitation from carbon monoxide poisoning occurs 3× faster in microgravity enclosure fires than in equivalent terrestrial room fires.
